hebelwert.vorsicht: Its residual (distance from the line) can be small precisely because it pulled the line to itself. So compare the line with and without the point.

f-test.titel: F test (analysis of variance and regression)
f-test.kurz: Is there any difference or effect at all? The F test checks as a whole. Regression: are all B zero at once? Analysis of variance: are all group means equal? In analysis of variance, F is the spread (mean square) between groups divided by that within.
f-test.beispiel: Three teaching methods: between 6.0, within 2.0. F = 3.0.
f-test.vorsicht: A significant F means: at least two means differ. Which ones, only pairwise comparisons show.
f-test.fachwoerter: mean square (sum of squared deviations divided by degrees of freedom, a measure of spread), null hypothesis (the assumption "no difference" that the test examines).

schrittweise-regression.kurz: How does a program choose predictors by itself? Stepwise regression adds or removes predictors by a statistical criterion, such as the p value. Often quoted: entry at .05, removal at .10.
schrittweise-regression.beispiel: Of 20 possible predictors of rent, four remain.
schrittweise-regression.vorsicht: The choice knows neither theory nor causes and depends on these data. Whether the predictors make sense or are causes stays open.

extrapolation.kurz: Does the prediction hold far outside the observed values? Predicting there is extrapolation. It is not very reliable: the confidence interval of the prediction widens the further x is from the mean of x, and the line need not hold there.
extrapolation.beispiel: Plants measured in weeks 1 to 8, 5 cm per week. Week 80 would give 400 cm.
extrapolation.vorsicht: A high R² does not change this.

zusammenhang-ursache.kurz: Does a relationship show that one thing brings about the other? Not by itself. B shows: on average more x goes with more or less y, at equal values of the other predictors in the model. That is an association. Causation does not follow; a common cause can also produce both.
zusammenhang-ursache.beispiel: More ice cream sales, more sunburn: both follow the sunshine.
zusammenhang-ursache.vorsicht: Data for areas show a relationship between areas, not for the individual people within.

lineares-modell.kurz: Can linear regression only describe straight lines? No. "Linear" refers to the parameters (the B): each B only multiplies a predictor, everything is added. With a quadratic term (x and x² as predictors) the model fits a curve.
lineares-modell.beispiel: Yield = 2 + 3x - 0.2x²: a curve, but a linear model.
lineares-modell.vorsicht: x² is just another predictor. Its test (Sig.) shows whether it is needed, because R² rises with every addition.

scheinregression.kurz: Does a high R² between two time series show a real relationship? Not necessarily. If both rise over time (trend), the result is spurious regression. Warning signs: very high R² and similar residuals (autocorrelation), Durbin-Watson near 0.
scheinregression.beispiel: Bicycles in city A and coffee imports of country B rise yearly: R² = .95.
scheinregression.vorsicht: Using year-to-year changes, R² drops clearly if it was only trend.
scheinregression.fachwoerter: Durbin-Watson (test value for autocorrelation: near 2 none, near 0 positive, near 4 negative).

prognoseguete.kurz: How well does a forecast hit? MAE: mean absolute error. MAPE: mean percentage error, divides by the observed value, infinite at zero. MASE: divides by the error of the naive forecast (last value) in the fitting period. Below 1 better, above 1 worse than that.
prognoseguete.vorsicht: For rare counts with zeros, MAPE is useless.

preisindex.kurz: How much dearer has the same shopping become? The Laspeyres index holds base-period quantities fixed, so only prices change. Base effect: the change from a year ago can fall although the index rises, if it rose more a year ago.
preisindex.beispiel: 10 loaves, 20 l milk. Base: 2 and 1, value 40. Now 2.4 and 1.2: value 48. Index 1.20.
preisindex.vorsicht: Fixed quantities do not capture buyers switching to cheaper goods.

anscombe-quartett.kurz: Is one figure enough to describe data? No. Anscombe's quartet: four data sets with nearly the same r, means and line, but different point clouds (line, arc, outlier, one point fixes everything). So look at the scatter plot.
anscombe-quartett.beispiel: r = .80 fits a cloud around a line and points on a curve.
anscombe-quartett.vorsicht: r measures only the straight-line part. A single point can lower r sharply: check it, do not delete it.

kovarianz.kurz: How strongly do two values rise or fall together? Covariance measures it unstandardized, so its value depends on the scale. The correlation r is the covariance divided by the product of the standard deviations and stays the same when units change.
kovarianz.beispiel: Height and weight: covariance 60 with height in cm, 0.6 in metres. r the same.
kovarianz.vorsicht: Covariance 0 only means: no straight-line relationship, not independence.
kovarianz.fachwoerter: standard deviation (typical distance of values from the mean).

punktbiseriale-korrelation.kurz: Is a group (0/1) related to a measurement? The point-biserial correlation is the Pearson correlation of a 0/1 variable with a number. Its test is the independent-samples t test (equal variances): same p, same size of t.
punktbiseriale-korrelation.beispiel: A = 0, B = 1, r = +.30: B has higher values on average. Swapped: -.30.
punktbiseriale-korrelation.vorsicht: The sign follows the coding. The biserial correlation is something else.

fisher-z.kurz: Why is the interval skewed around r? r can be 1 at most, so at high r there is less room above. Fisher Z makes the distribution of r roughly normal. The interval is built in Z and converted back, so it is asymmetric.
fisher-z.vorsicht: The interval is never the probability of the true value. Fisher Z is not z standardization.

fehlerarten.titel: Type I and type II errors (α, β)
fehlerarten.kurz: Can a test be wrong? Yes, twice over. Type I error: no difference, yet “significant”. Type II error: a difference exists but is missed. The level α (often .05) is the rate of the first error when nothing is there.
fehlerarten.beispiel: 200 tests with no real difference, α = .05: about 10 falsely significant.
fehlerarten.vorsicht: α does not say whether a single finding is wrong. A type II error has probability β = 1 minus power.
fehlerarten.fachwoerter: Power (the chance of finding a difference that exists), level (the limit for p chosen in advance).

einseitig-zweiseitig.kurz: Does one direction count, or both? Two-sided asks: is there a difference, in either direction? One-sided asks only: is A larger than B? The same data can be significant one-sided, not two-sided. When in doubt, test two-sided.
einseitig-zweiseitig.beispiel: New teaching method: two-sided p = .08, one-sided p = .04.
einseitig-zweiseitig.vorsicht: The direction must be fixed before looking at the data. Choosing it afterwards halves p without new information.

mehrfaches-testen.kurz: How often does chance fool you across many tests? At level .05, each test gives a false alarm 5 percent of the time when nothing is real. Across m independent tests, the chance of at least one is 1 - .95 to the power m (alpha inflation). Bonferroni divides the level by m.
mehrfaches-testen.beispiel: 10 tests, nothing real: about 40 percent chance of a hit.
mehrfaches-testen.vorsicht: About m times .05 chance hits. Searching yields only hypotheses.

effekt-ueberschaetzung.kurz: Is a significant effect as large as measured? Often not. If only significant results count, estimates are biased upward: a small study becomes significant only with a luckily large estimate. This is the winner’s curse.
effekt-ueberschaetzung.beispiel: True difference medium-sized. Of many small studies only the significant ones appear; their average lies above it.
effekt-ueberschaetzung.vorsicht: The smaller the study, the stronger the bias. Replications therefore often find smaller effects, not necessarily zero.
effekt-ueberschaetzung.fachwoerter: significant (the p value is below the chosen limit, usually .05).

falsch-positive-befunde.titel: False positive findings (type I error, researcher degrees of freedom)
falsch-positive-befunde.kurz: How many significant findings are false alarms? It depends on level, power and the share of real effects. With low power the false share rises. More false alarms also arise when you test after every new case and stop at significance, or try many analyses and report only the successful one (researcher degrees of freedom).
falsch-positive-befunde.beispiel: 1000 effects tested, 100 real, power .5, level .05: 50 true and 45 false hits.
falsch-positive-befunde.vorsicht: The level .05 holds only for a sample and analysis planned in advance. The rate rises even without intent to deceive.
falsch-positive-befunde.fachwoerter: power (the chance of finding a real effect), level (the limit for p set in advance), significant (p is below this limit).

fehlerbalken.kurz: What do the bars at the means show? That is not fixed: standard deviation (spread of single values), standard error (precision of the mean) or confidence interval. "± number" does not tell which. One standard error either side is about half as wide as the 95 percent interval and corresponds to about 68 percent.
fehlerbalken.vorsicht: Overlap does not decide; the test of the difference does. If the 95 percent intervals share no range, independent groups differ significantly at the .05 level. For paired measurements, the interval of the differences per person counts, not the intervals of the two means.

levene-test.kurz: Do the groups spread equally? (Levene test) It checks whether the variance, the spread of the values, is the same across groups. A small p points to unequal spread.
levene-test.beispiel: Two groups of 8 people each, Levene p = .40: no sign of unequal spread.
levene-test.vorsicht: Not significant does not mean the spread is equal. With small groups the test detects differences poorly. It does not prove equality.

gepoolter-t-test.titel: Pooled spread or Welch test (equal spread assumed?)
gepoolter-t-test.kurz: Do both groups spread equally? The t test with pooled (combined) spread assumes so. The Welch test does not combine and adjusts the degrees of freedom. With two groups, F of the analysis of variance is the square of t, with the same p.
gepoolter-t-test.beispiel: 10 people with spread 8, 40 with spread 3: pooling mostly reflects the large group with the small spread.
gepoolter-t-test.vorsicht: If the smaller group spreads more, the pooled test shows significance too often. Welch corrects this.
gepoolter-t-test.fachwoerter: Degrees of freedom (a number that fixes the reference distribution of t).

zentraler-grenzwertsatz.kurz: Must values be normally distributed? Not always. The central limit theorem says: means of many observations are approximately normal, even when single values are skewed. It applies to means, not to single values.
zentraler-grenzwertsatz.beispiel: Incomes are skewed. Means of 200 people each lie almost symmetrically.
zentraler-grenzwertsatz.vorsicht: How many suffice depends on the shape: with strongly skewed values, 10 is not enough. With large groups, t tests are usually usable without normally distributed values.

pseudoreplikation.kurz: Does every value count as separate information? No, if values belong together. Pseudoreplication: dependent values are treated as independent, such as repeated measurements of one person or children of one class. The standard error gets too small; significance appears too often.
pseudoreplikation.beispiel: 20 plants, 5 leaves measured on each: that is 20 independent units, not 100.
pseudoreplikation.vorsicht: More rows are not more information. Remedy: one mean per unit, or a model that accounts for the grouping.
pseudoreplikation.fachwoerter: standard error (how much an estimate typically varies), significant (the p value is below the chosen limit, usually .05).

simpson-paradox.kurz: Can a relationship flip when groups are pooled? Yes. The overall picture can hide or reverse what each group shows (Simpson’s paradox, also for the correlation r). Reason: the groups differ in the measures or in make-up.
simpson-paradox.beispiel: A helps more than B in mild and in severe cases. But A goes almost only to severe cases. Overall, A looks worse.
simpson-paradox.vorsicht: The total cannot then be read directly. Which view applies depends on the situation.

erwartete-haeufigkeit.kurz: How many cases per cell would be expected if the variables were unrelated? Row total times column total divided by the grand total. The chi-square test compares them with the observed counts. Which cell stands out shows only in the per-cell comparison.
erwartete-haeufigkeit.vorsicht: Commonly cited: all at least 5, a habit. With smaller values in a 2x2 table, use Fisher’s exact test.
erwartete-haeufigkeit.fachwoerter: Cross-tab (table of two variables), standardized residual (gap between observed and expected, scaled to be comparable).

zeilenprozent.kurz: What share within one group? In a cross-tab, row percent is cell count divided by row total, times 100. The row total is the reference. “What percent of A have B?” takes the total of A as reference. Column percent uses the column total.
zeilenprozent.beispiel: 80 dog owners, 20 of them also with a cat: 20 / 80 = 25 percent.
zeilenprozent.vorsicht: Row and column percent are different numbers. First ask: share of what?

likelihood-ratio.kurz: How much does a test result change the estimate? The positive LR is sensitivity divided by (1 minus specificity): that many times more often a positive result occurs in the sick than in the healthy. Above 1 favors the disease. Post-test odds = pre-test odds times LR.
likelihood-ratio.beispiel: Pre-test .20, so odds .25. LR 4 gives odds 1, which is .50.
likelihood-ratio.vorsicht: LR is not a probability. Back to p: odds divided by (1 plus odds).
likelihood-ratio.fachwoerter: Sensitivity (share of the sick the test detects), specificity (share of the healthy it correctly calls healthy), odds (p divided by 1 minus p).

regelkarte.kurz: Has the process changed? A control chart plots group means in order, with a center line and limits, often ±3 standard errors. A point outside is a signal: probably more than chance is at work. Phase 1 estimates limits from past data, phase 2 then monitors continuously. CUSUM and EWMA combine several groups and detect small, lasting shifts sooner.
regelkarte.beispiel: Stable: about 3 in 1000 points outside. Several in short succession are a clear signal.
regelkarte.vorsicht: If a stable process stays inside the limits, the variation is chance: adjusting then increases the spread. Limits from few groups are imprecise.
regelkarte.fachwoerter: Standard error (spread of the group means), stable (the distribution stays the same over time).

prozessfaehigkeit.kurz: Does the process meet the specification? Cp compares the allowed range with the spread and ignores where the mean lies. Cpk measures the distance from the mean to the nearer limit, at most as large as Cp. Both assume a stable, normal process.
prozessfaehigkeit.beispiel: Cp = 1, centered: about 0.27 percent outside; shifted, more.
prozessfaehigkeit.vorsicht: Cp = 1 only means: not fewer than 0.27 percent outside. With control chart signals the index says little; clear them first.

messsystem.kurz: How much spread comes from measuring itself? Repeatability: spread of the device on the same unit, same operator, same setup. Reproducibility: spread between operators, setups or periods. Measurement share of the total spread = 1 minus process share. The signal-to-noise ratio shows how well parts can be told apart: often cited, 5 or more good, below 2 useless.
messsystem.beispiel: Process 80 percent of the spread: measurement system 20 percent.
messsystem.vorsicht: Authors assign the terms differently, so the definition used must be stated. The limits are conventions.

versuchsplanung.kurz: How to plan experiments that show a lot? Interaction: the effect of one factor depends on the level of another. Changing one factor at a time cannot estimate it; all combinations find it. A repeated center point shows curvature and estimates the spread.
versuchsplanung.beispiel: Fertilizer works strongly in sun, hardly in shade.
versuchsplanung.vorsicht: A result at one level does not automatically hold for all. With curvature, two levels are not enough; the design can be extended.
versuchsplanung.fachwoerter: Factor (a quantity you set on purpose), level (one set value of it), continuous (every value in between is possible).
